The fluorescent lights of the dilapidated row house flickered, casting an eerie glow over the cramped living room. Dust motes danced in the stale air as Malik paced back and forth, phone pressed to his ear. 

"Nah man, I ain't got that re-up ready yet. The connect's been layin' low, you feel me?" He ran a hand over his closely shaved head, brow furrowed in frustration. 

A baby wailed from the back bedroom, the thin walls doing little to muffle the piercing cries. Malik winced, shooting an annoyed glance down the hallway.

"Look, I'll have it for you tomorrow, a'ight? Jus' gotta work this out." He listened for a moment, jaw clenching. "Nah, nah, I got it covered. You know I ain't gon' let you down."

Ending the call, Malik shoved the phone into his pocket and sank down onto the sagging couch. He stared ahead blankly, the sound of the baby's cries wearing on his nerves. This was the life he'd chosen - a constant hustle, a daily grind of keeping all the pieces in place. One wrong move and everything could come crashing down.

He closed his eyes, letting out a weary sigh. The weight of the streets was heavy, but he had no other choice. Survival was the name of the game here, and he was determined to come out on top.
